corrected_draft.title: Trump Orders Detention Pending Immigration Removal Proceedings
corrected_draft.description_short: On January 20, 2025, Trump’s immigration executive order directed detention pending removal proceedings or removal to the extent permitted by law.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Protecting the American People Against Invasion.” The order directed the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that noncitizens apprehended under specified provisions are detained pending further proceedings regarding their removal or removal from the United States, to the extent permitted by law. The text does not establish unlimited or indefinite detention without charge.
corrected_draft.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed the executive order “Protecting the American People Against Invasion.” The order directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to ensure that noncitizens apprehended under specified provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act are detained pending further proceedings regarding their removal from the United States, or removal from the country, to the extent permitted by law. The source supports a discrete executive action and its stated detention directive. It does not say that the president created a new authority for indefinite detention without charge, and its express “to the extent permitted by law” language limits the directive. A corrected title and description should describe the order’s stated instruction without turning it into a claim that it eliminated legal protections or established detention without judicial process.
